patches.beforeText: Temple3 is a v0.1 laboratory. It is not a production system, and it has not been independently audited.
patches.html: This gate is an educational miniature. Its witnesses belong to this page; they do not certify a production platform or independently audit Temple.
patches.subject: ms.temple.index.html.n1309

patches.beforeText: 101 of 101 checks passed in its latest integrated qualification run.
patches.html: The original laboratory reported qualification checks. Those results describe that prototype, rather than the current state of every Temple implementation.
patches.subject: ms.temple.index.html.n1314

patches.beforeText: Three implementations — a JavaScript model, a Python verifier and a Rust library — are cross-checked on shared vectors. They share design lineage, so correlated mistakes remain possible.
patches.html: The original laboratory compared three implementations — JavaScript, Python and Rust. Shared design lineage means correlated mistakes remain possible.
patches.subject: ms.temple.index.html.n1319

patches.beforeText: 486 hostile cases in a differential corpus surfaced 26 semantic mismatches between them. After repair: zero.
patches.html: Adversarial cases were used to compare implementations and expose differences in how they judged the same proposals.
patches.subject: ms.temple.index.html.n1324

patches.beforeText: Two Temples have federated in the lab. Networking, key rotation, encryption and zero-knowledge proofs are not built.
patches.html: An original two-Temple demonstration explored federation and recovery. It was a laboratory exercise, not a production networking or security system.
patches.subject: ms.temple.index.html.n1329

patches.beforeText: Today, Sourcery and Claimipedia run on Temple2 — the fact runtime Temple3 learns from.
patches.html: This published edition runs the miniature through process algebra. The wider corpus holds the design notes and implementation history.

patches.beforeText: No cameras and no stock footage: a sky computed pixel by pixel, lights that leave trails, the commandments set in type, and a drone synthesised from sine waves. Every frame can be rendered again from the site’s own source — and the film carries a witness of its own.

patches.html: The Covenant · 41 seconds · 1280×720 · retained from the original procedural film.
patches.subject: ms.temple.films/index.html.n97

patches.beforeText: The film is a separate pipeline beside the site. A choreography file sets every scene, plate, light, spark and chime to the tenth of a second; one Python script turns it into picture and sound with ffmpeg and headless Chrome.
patches.html: The original film was made with a separate rendering pipeline. A choreography file set the scenes, lights, sparks and chimes; Python, ffmpeg and headless Chrome produced the picture and sound. This edition retains the rendered files and their manifest.
patches.subject: ms.temple.films/index.html.n153

patches.beforeText: Every file below carries the hash of its bytes, and the whole set carries the hash of the sources that produced it. The site’s tests recompute both: change a single frame’s recipe without re-rendering, and the build refuses to call the film current.
patches.html: The manifest records the original files and the source hash reported by their rendering pipeline. This edition checks the retained file bytes against the captured hashes. It does not rerun or independently verify that original rendering pipeline.
patches.subject: ms.temple.films/index.html.n253

patches.beforeText: A speculative design. The film was rendered from code by ffmpeg and headless Chrome; its recipe lives beside the site’s source.
patches.html: A speculative design, retained from the original procedural film. The published media are checked against their captured file hashes.
patches.subject: ms.temple.films/index.html.n347

patches.beforeText: The pipeline hashes its own sources and every file it renders. The site’s tests recompute both, so a film that no longer matches its sources can’t slip through unnoticed.
patches.html: The original pipeline recorded hashes for its sources and rendered files. This edition preserves the film and checks its published bytes against the captured file hashes; it does not rerun the original rendering pipeline.
